---
title: v3.1.1 — Physical Skill Entries and Explicit Runtime Paths
---

## Overview

Replace link-based Host Skill discovery with physical entry files on Windows and macOS, eliminating reliance on junctions, symbolic links and the project's working directory when locating installed Runtime resources.

## Highlights

- Generate physical Work and Tooling SKILL.md entries in the fixed Codex and Claude Code discovery directories. Inject absolute paths to the shared bootstrap, Skill root, required CLI binaries and installation state; retain source templates in release packages without installing duplicate entry files in the Runtime tree.
- Include both generated entries in the installation SHA-256 manifest and the existing installation transaction. Preserve safe reinstall, interruption recovery, cross-drive publication, custom installation paths and third-party Skill protection.
- Reject linked managed Skill resources in the Rust source store, including aliases within the same boundary. Replace the obsolete link_escape error with unsafe_link while retaining source boundaries, Shared deduplication and incremental loading.
- Remove link-specific installation and rollback logic, dedicated non-administrator smoke tests and obsolete fixtures and reporting fields. Preserve normal installation, user-level locks, integrity checks and Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility.
- Validate actual generated entry paths from a non-installation working directory using automated Host simulation, alongside Windows and macOS installation, package, downloader and Rust regression tests.

## Upgrade Note

Existing installations that use junctions or symbolic links, and unfinished transactions from the previous installation format, are not migrated automatically. Resolve unfinished installer transactions with the previous release, confirm ownership and back up or manually remove only the previous managed resources before a fresh installation. Do not delete unknown entries, link targets containing unrelated data, or third-party Skills. See the installation guide for safe handling.

The Host simulation is automated validation, not a live Codex or Claude Code compatibility test.
